blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Rank counts only communities with at least ten homes listed. Falling listings with steady sales mean homes are being absorbed faster; rising listings with steady sales mean more choice for buyers. A sellers’ best bet is a community where homes sell quickly against the number listed; a buyers’ best bet is the reverse. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal.

blocks.text: Between June 2026 and October 2026, detached houses: listings rose from 20 in June to 28 in October (+40.0%), and it took 5.3% of the city’s 357 sales over the period; condos and townhomes: listings was little changed, 3 in June and 3 in October (+0.0%), and it took 0.3% of the city’s 694 sales over the period.
The monthly write-ups singled out Salmon River for detached houses in June, September (a sellers’ best bet); detached houses in October (a buyers’ best bet).

blocks.text: Lots and land in Salmon River
Fee-simple parcels

items.t: Valley-floor parcels: farm and acreage houses on large rural lots along the river valley, under the Township Rural Plan designations and Zoning Bylaw No. 2500; the district's farm and acreage homes sit in the rural zones, including RU-2. Lot character as stated: large rural parcels — typical lot sizes from direct Bylaw 2500 text were not confirmed, and the RU-2 minimum lot area and frontage were not confirmed from a readable bylaw section: both not confirmed, no size invented here.

Upland parcels (56 Avenue / Rawlison Crescent side): the same fee-simple acreage form on the upland side of the district — horse owners using the upland lots are part of the typical-buyer picture. No separate upland zone minimum is stated: Not confirmed lot-by-lot.

Strata vs freehold, as stated: most Salmon River properties are non-strata freehold acreages; where a strata parcel exists, BC strata law is the Strata Property Act. (SnapStats FVR September 2026 report.)
ALR vs non-ALR split: farm land in the valley is in the Agricultural Land Reserve in places; no percentage split is available. Confirm a specific parcel on the ALC maps.

Serviced vs unserviced — well/septic ground, as stated: rural properties may use wells — search GWELLS, the provincial database of registered wells and mapped aquifers, for a parcel's record (well reports due within 90 days of constructing, altering or decommissioning a well). No municipal water/sewer position for valley parcels is stated — treat the district as well/septic diligence ground unless the Township confirms otherwise for the parcel.

Flood character of the land itself: the Salmon River valley is Fraser River floodplain land — the Township states the Salmon River Pump Station was originally built to help mitigate flooding of the surrounding agricultural lands during freshet, provides flood protection when Fraser River levels rise, and has flood box gates that close as river levels rise. Valley-floor land value is inseparable from that system.

Riparian character: the Salmon River is salmon-bearing, so setbacks and riparian rules can limit building envelopes near the river — parcel-level setback distances: Not confirmed; check with the Township before planning a build. Price buildable area, not gross area.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Salmon River

items.t: Municipality: Township of Langley, BC — Salmon River is the rural district along the Salmon River in the township's northwest, north of the Otter area and south of Fort Langley.
MLS sub-area name as the board uses it: "Salmon River" (Fraser Valley Real Estate Board data in the SnapStats FVR September 2026 report).

The district follows the Salmon River valley between 232 Street and 264 Street, from the Fraser River side south toward 40 Avenue, with Rawlison Crescent and 56 Avenue on the upland side; no Township-published boundary for the sub-area was confirmed.
The name is the river's name: the Salmon River is a salmon-bearing watercourse, and Metro Vancouver watershed material covers the Salmon River watershed.
Nearby areas: Fort Langley to the north, Otter District to the south, Walnut Grove to the west, Aldergrove to the southeast.

Main roads and commute: 56 Avenue and Rawlison Crescent on the upland, 232 Street and 240 Street as the north–south edges, and River Road / Glover Road toward Fort Langley; Highway 1 access is south via the 200 Street or 232 Street interchanges; there is no SkyTrain or West Coast Express station in the district.

Transit: TransLink route 562 (Walnut Grove / Langley Centre) runs on Glover Road via 96 Avenue, 88 Avenue and 202 Street to Carvolth Exchange, serving the Fort Langley edge of the district; no TransLink route was confirmed on 56 Avenue, Rawlison Crescent or the valley roads inside the district.

Schools: catchments are address-based in SD35. For the sample address 4452 256 Street, the SD35 School Locator returns Elementary — North Otter Elementary; Middle — none shown by the locator; Secondary — D.W. Poppy Secondary; other addresses may fall in different catchments, and no home is promised a specific school. Coghlan Fundamental Elementary, 4452 256 Street, a district school of choice, stands on the upland east side; its position inside this board sub-area is not confirmed. No SD35 school physically inside the Salmon River valley itself was confirmed.

Parks/facilities: the Salmon River Natural Area is a Township park listed among the Fort Langley-area parks; no recreation centre or library branch inside the district was confirmed — the nearest Township facilities are in Fort Langley and Walnut Grove.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Salmon River

items.t: Zoning + plans: rural land is under Township of Langley Zoning Bylaw No. 2500 (rural zones, including RU-2; RU-2 minimum lot area/frontage not confirmed from a readable section; zone assignments for a parcel come from the bylaw Map Schedules through the Township's GeoSource). The Township Official Community Plan and the Rural Plan govern the district.
SSMUH in the Township: Bylaw 6020 (adopted November 18, 2024), with no six-unit tier. Suite cap 120 m².

Coach house: fee-simple, never strata. A coach house is a fee-simple second unit under Zoning Bylaw 2500 s.102, where a "coach house" is an accessory dwelling unit located only within the second storey of a detached garage. It is never a strata unit.

R-CL s.403 (where it applies): 220 m² minimum / 464.5 m² maximum under Zoning Bylaw 2500 s.403 — carried as the Township standing position; R-CL is a Willoughby-form zone and its application to any Salmon River parcel is not confirmed. Willoughby Plan = Bylaw 1836 (1979), now Schedule 6 to Bylaw 6200 (standing position; Willoughby is a different community — do not apply its plan to Salmon River ground).
Flood / pump-station diligence: Flood status drives insurance and lending on these parcels.

ALR rules (valley farm land in the ALR, in places): subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s.6; SPA s.239; ALCA s.21(1)); ALC residence caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha) — the ALC permits one additional residence without an ALC application where its size rules are met, subject to Township bylaws; BC Assessment farm-class thresholds in full three-tier form ($2,500 on 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 + 5% of value over 4 ha; $10,000 under 0.8 ha; applications by Oct 31) — a flat "$2,500+" line is an error.
Federal non-Canadian purchase prohibition — vacant land: Get advice on the current official text for the specific parcel.

blocks.text: Good to know about Salmon River

items.t: The pump station is the valley's defining infrastructure: the Salmon River Pump Station has flood box gates that close as Fraser River levels rise, and Council has authorized detailed design and tendering for its upgrades — a live Township project a valley-floor buyer should read before valuing land inside the dykes.
Poppy Secondary, which is why "the school at the address" and "the catchment for the address" are different questions here. No SD35 school physically inside the valley itself was confirmed.

Health care is outside the district: Langley Memorial Hospital, 22051 Fraser Highway, Langley, is the Fraser Health community hospital with 24/7 emergency serving the area, southwest of the district; the Langley Urgent and Primary Care Centre is at 202 – 20434 64th Avenue, Langley. No hospital or clinic inside the district was confirmed.

Listings tagged Salmon River can include Langley City condos. A 1-bedroom condo at "Cornerstone North by Marcon" near Kwantlen Polytechnic University is labelled "Salmon River" in the listing feed, but it is Langley City product, not Salmon River land, and shouldn't be compared with acreages.

blocks.text: Duplexes and half duplexes in Salmon River
What a duplex looks like in Salmon River

items.t: The usual duplex form: Rural land sits under Zoning Bylaw No. 2500 (the district's farm and acreage homes sit in the rural zones, including RU-2); the RU-2 minimum lot area and frontage were not confirmed from a readable bylaw section: Not verified; zone assignments for a parcel come from the bylaw Map Schedules through the Township's GeoSource.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect duplexes in Salmon River

items.t: ALR and flood — the governing facts for the valley floor: Farm land in the valley is in the Agricultural Land Reserve in places; confirm a specific parcel on the ALC maps. On ALR land the ALC permits one additional residence without an ALC application where its size rules are met — up to 90 m² on properties of 40 ha or less and up to 186 m² on properties over 40 ha — subject to Township bylaws; the principal residence maximum is 500 m² and a secondary suite must be entirely inside the principal residence. The Salmon River valley is Fraser River floodplain land — the Township states the Salmon River Pump Station was originally built to help mitigate flooding of the surrounding agricultural lands during freshet, provides flood protection when Fraser River levels rise, and has flood box gates that close as river levels rise; Council has authorized staff to proceed with detailed design and tendering for the Pump Station Upgrades. Parcel-level floodplain mapping and watercourse setback distances for a specific parcel are not verified — the Salmon River is salmon-bearing, so setbacks and riparian rules can limit building envelopes near the river; check with the Township before planning a build.

faq.q: What kind of land actually sells in Salmon River?
faq.a: Large fee-simple rural parcels — valley-floor farm land and 56 Avenue / Rawlison Crescent upland acreages — parcel by parcel.

faq.q: Is the land in the ALR?
faq.a: Farm land in the valley is in the Agricultural Land Reserve in places; confirm a specific parcel on the ALC ALR maps before assuming a farm use, a second dwelling or a subdivision is possible.

faq.q: Is the valley in a floodplain?
faq.a: Yes — the valley is Fraser River floodplain land; the Township states the Salmon River Pump Station provides flood protection when Fraser River levels rise and was built to mitigate flooding of the surrounding agricultural lands during freshet.

faq.q: Can I subdivide a big parcel?
faq.a: Get the zone confirmed through the Township's GeoSource Map Schedules before writing on split potential.

faq.q: Is there a duplex development in Salmon River I can buy into?
faq.a: The documented stock is non-strata freehold acreages and rural houses, some with suites; price a suite as a suite under the 120 m² Township cap, not as a duplex half.

faq.q: Are Cedar Springs or Westfield Courts duplex or ownership stock?
faq.a: No — both are tenure records on the pad-rental side, documented at their Salmon River mobile home. A home on a rented pad there would be a chattel on rented land, never duplex stock.

faq.q: Is the Salmon River district in a floodplain?
faq.a: The valley is Fraser River floodplain land; the Township states the Pump Station provides flood protection when river levels rise, and upgrades are in detailed design and tendering. Parcel-level floodplain mapping is not verified — flood status drives insurance and lending, so check the specific parcel.

faq.q: Which schools serve a Salmon River address?
faq.a: Poppy Secondary — that address only, never transferred. No SD35 school physically inside the valley itself was confirmed. Run the exact address before promising a school.
Route 562 runs on Glover Road at the Fort Langley edge of the district, between Langley Centre and Walnut Grove / Carvolth Exchange; no route inside the valley roads was confirmed.

faq.q: Can an acreage add a second dwelling?
faq.a: On ALR land the ALC permits one additional residence without an ALC application where its size rules are met (up to 90 m² at 40 ha or less, up to 186 m² over 40 ha), subject to Township bylaws; the Township's small-scale multi-unit rules also allow a suite or accessory unit on lots over 4,050 m² depending on zoning.
